business_question: At booking, before the vendor is paid, which consignments will lose money?

base_rate_or_baseline.metric: PR-AUC of constant base rate (= test prevalence)

extra_baselines.name: Rate-card lookup (route×vendor×vehicle_type, fitted on train, <5 rows -> train base rate)

winner_reason: LightGBM chosen on PR-AUC (0.7429); models within 2% of the best: ['LightGBM'] (simplest preferred). LightGBM beats the rate-card lookup by 0.161 PR-AUC (>= 0.03), so the model adds signal beyond the lane-vendor rate card so the 'renegotiate the rate card, not prediction' conclusion does not apply.

top_drivers.plain_english: Higher shipment_utilisation lowers the predicted loss risk.
route: the biggest push toward loss risk comes from 'PGDAD1', the biggest push away from it from 'GCHAZ2'.
vehicle_type: the biggest push toward loss risk comes from 'SB01', the biggest push away from it from 'SB04'.
vendor_name: the biggest push toward loss risk comes from 'V009', the biggest push away from it from 'V051'.
month matters, but not in one direction: its effect depends on the lane and vehicle.

caveats: 560 exact duplicate rows (all 69 columns equal; ₹1.1 Cr of freight, 322 shipments) were dropped before modelling; see data/processed/audit_duplicate_rows.csv.
One client sector (polyester), one year of data.
Threshold 0.5345 was selected on the Oct-Dec 2025 validation slice (precision 0.600, recall 0.741 there) and applied unchanged to test, where precision is 0.597 and recall 0.839.
shipment_utilisation and n_lrs are shipment-level and may not be known at booking; without them LightGBM PR-AUC is 0.673 (rate-card lookup 0.5814).
RandomForest fitted on a 50,000-row training sample.
